claims.text: Localized laser cladding of a pre-alloyed Ni-based coating with ceramic reinforcements will reduce hot-cracking risk relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The laser-clad coating will increase surface hardness relative to both traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The laser-clad coating will improve wear resistance relative to both traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The laser-clad coating will improve corrosion resistance relative to both traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
Laser cladding produces rapid, localized melting with lower heat input when laser power, scan speed, and shielding gas are controlled.
The proposed laser-cladding process will produce a finely grained microstructure.
The proposed coating will have a graded interface containing well-dispersed ceramic particulates.
The ceramic particulates will reduce internal residual stresses.
The ceramic particulates will inhibit crack nucleation.
The rapid heating and cooling cycle of laser cladding refines the grain structure.
Localized laser cladding minimizes the size of the heat-affected zone.
Grain refinement and a smaller heat-affected zone reduce the propensity for hot cracking.
Embedded ceramic reinforcements increase mechanical hardness.
Embedded ceramic reinforcements impede crack propagation.
Embedded ceramic reinforcements improve wear resistance.
Embedded ceramic reinforcements improve corrosion resistance.
